title: Main Theorem
body_md:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $\mathscr X$ be a smooth locally reductive algebraic stack of finite type over $k$, with separated diagonal. Suppose that $\mathscr X$ admits an adequate moduli
space $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$. Then only finitely many open substacks of $\mathscr X$ preserve $\pi$. Their reduced boundaries are unions of prime divisors taken from a fixed finite collection, and the collections of divisors that can be removed simultaneously form a finite simplicial complex determined by boundary weights.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: One of the main difficulties in proving \textbf{Main Theorem} lies in identifying the correct characterization of the boundary. This is achieved by verifying many artificially constructed quotient stacks, especially those arising from torus actions. Once this is done, the generalization to locally reductive stacks is fairly straightforward. A distinctive feature of the proof is its combination of classical and modern methods: GIT handles the local case (quotient stacks), while stack-theoretic machinery handles the global case (locally reductive stacks).
head: environment

title: Conventions
body_md:
All algebraic stacks and algebraic spaces are quasi-separated.
A variety is a separated scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field. A reductive group scheme is a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation with connected reductive geometric fibers.
head: manual

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space. An open substack $\mathscr U \subseteq \mathscr X$ is said to \emph{preserve $\pi$} if the restriction $\pi|_{\mathscr U}: \mathscr U \to X$ is an adequate moduli space. Equivalently, the open substack $\mathscr U$ admits an adequate moduli space $\mathscr U \to U$ and the induced morphism between adequate moduli spaces
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathscr U \ar[r,hook] \ar[d] & \mathscr X \ar[d,"\pi"] \\
U \ar[r,"\sim"] & X
\end{tikzcd}
\]
is an isomorphism. Denote by $\operatorname{Op}(\pi)$ the set of open substacks of $\mathscr X$ preserving $\pi$, including $\mathscr X$ itself.

A closed substack $\mathscr D \subseteq \mathscr X$ is called \emph{removable} for $\pi$ if its open complement $\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr D \subseteq \mathscr X$ preserves $\pi$.

label: lem:gerbe
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gerbe}
Let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space, and let $f: \mathscr Y \to \mathscr X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated fppf gerbe, banded by a linearly reductive group scheme over $\mathscr X$. Then $\pi \circ f: \mathscr Y \to X$ is an adequate moduli space. Moreover, pullback along $f$ induces a bijection between the open substacks preserving $\pi$ and those preserving $\pi \circ f$.
head: environment
name: Preserving opens through a gerbe

title: Proof
body_md:
We first show that $\pi \circ f$ is an adequate moduli space. Fppf locally on $\mathscr X$, the gerbe $f$ is of the form $\mathscr X \times \mathrm{B}G \to \mathscr X$. Linear reductivity of $G$ implies that $f_*$ is exact on quasi-coherent modules and $f_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}=\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Thus $f$ is cohomologically affine, and $\pi \circ f$ is adequately affine by
\cite[Prop. 4.2.1 (1)--(2)]{AlperAdequate}. Since $(\pi \circ f)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y} \simeq \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X} \simeq \mathcal O_X$, the composition $\pi \circ f$ is an adequate moduli space.

A gerbe is a universal homeomorphism \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06R9}{Tag 06R9}]{stacks-project}. So every open substack $\mathscr U \subseteq \mathscr Y$ is of the form $f^{-1}(\mathscr V)$ for some unique open substack $\mathscr V \subseteq \mathscr X$. Let
\[
f_{\mathscr V}: \mathscr U \to \mathscr V \text{ and } \pi_{\mathscr V}:=\pi|_{\mathscr V}.
\]
The above arguments apply to $f_{\mathscr V}$. In particular, if $\mathscr V$ preserves $\pi$, then $\mathscr U$ preserves $\pi \circ f$.

Conversely, suppose that $\pi_{\mathscr V} \circ f_{\mathscr V}: \mathscr U \to X$ is an adequate moduli space. Then $(\pi_{\mathscr V})_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr V} \simeq (\pi_{\mathscr V} \circ f_{\mathscr V})_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr U} \simeq \mathcal O_X$. To check adequate affineness, let $\mathcal{A} \twoheadrightarrow \mathcal B$ be a surjection of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathscr V}$-algebras. Using the adequate affineness of $\pi_{\mathscr V} \circ f_{\mathscr V}$, we obtain a
universally adequate homomorphism
\[
(\pi_{\mathscr V} \circ f_{\mathscr V})_* \circ f_{\mathscr V}^*\mathcal{A} \to (\pi_{\mathscr V} \circ f_{\mathscr V})_* \circ f_{\mathscr V}^*\mathcal B.
\]
The adjunction isomorphisms identify this homomorphism with $(\pi_{\mathscr V})_*\mathcal{A} \to (\pi_{\mathscr V})_*\mathcal B$. Hence $\pi_{\mathscr V}$ is adequately affine and therefore
an adequate moduli space.

label: lem:affine-open
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:affine-open}
Let $\mathscr X$ be an algebraic stack with affine diagonal, and let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space. If an open immersion $j: \mathscr U \hookrightarrow \mathscr X$ preserves $\pi$, then $j$ is affine.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Affineness of $j$ can be checked after an \'{e}tale covering of $X$, and adequate moduli spaces are preserved by \'{e}tale base change. We may assume that $X$ is affine. Because $\pi$ is quasi-compact, $\mathscr X$ is quasi-compact, so it admits a smooth surjective atlas $p: Y \to \mathscr X$ with $Y$ affine. To conclude, we show the base change $j_Y: Y \times_\mathscr X \mathscr U \to Y$ is affine. First we show that $p$ is affine. Consider the Cartesian diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
Y \ar[r,"\Gamma_p"] \ar[d] & Y \times_X \mathscr X \ar[r] \ar[d] & Y \ar[d,"p"'] & Y \times_\mathscr X \mathscr U \ar[d,"p_{\mathscr U}"] \ar[l,hook,"j_Y"'] \\
\mathscr X \ar[r,"\Delta_\pi"'] & \mathscr X \times_X \mathscr X \ar[r] \ar[d] & \mathscr X \ar[d,"\pi"] & \mathscr U \ar[l,hook,"j"] \\
& \mathscr X \ar[r,"\pi"'] & X
\end{tikzcd}
\]
So the atlas $p: Y \to \mathscr X$ factors as $Y \xrightarrow{\Gamma_p} Y \times_X \mathscr X \xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2} \mathscr X$. The graph $\Gamma_p$ is a base change of the diagonal $\Delta_\pi$ of $\pi$, which is again a base change of the diagonal of $\mathscr X$, so is affine.  The second projection $\mathrm{pr}_2$ is a base change of $\pi \circ p: Y \to X$, which is affine as both $Y$ and $X$ are affine. Thus $p$ is affine. Then the morphism $p_{\mathscr U}: Y \times_{\mathscr X} \mathscr U \to \mathscr U$ is affine. Note that $\pi|_{\mathscr U}: \mathscr U \to X$ is qcqs. Consequently, the composition $Y \times_{\mathscr X} \mathscr U \xrightarrow{p_{\mathscr U}} \mathscr U
\xrightarrow{\pi|_{\mathscr U}} X$ is adequately affine and qcqs, and hence affine \cite[Thm. 4.3.1]{AlperAdequate}. Since $X$ is affine, $Y \times_{\mathscr X} \mathscr U$ is also affine. Then $j_Y: Y \times_{\mathscr X} \mathscr U \to Y$ is a morphism between affine schemes, hence affine.
head: environment

label: cor:affine-test
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:affine-test}
Let $\mathscr X$ be an algebraic stack with affine diagonal, and let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space. Then an open immersion $j: \mathscr U \hookrightarrow \mathscr X$ preserves
$\pi$ if and only if $j$ is affine and the canonical map
$\mathcal O_X \to (\pi \circ j)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr U}$ is an isomorphism.

label: lem:boundary-purity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:boundary-purity}
Let $\mathscr X$ be a locally noetherian algebraic stack with affine diagonal, and let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space. Let $j: \mathscr U \hookrightarrow \mathscr X$ be a non-trivial open immersion preserving $\pi$. If $j$ is dense (e.g., if $\mathscr X$ is irreducible or normal), then the boundary $\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr U$ is pure of codimension $1$. If $\mathscr X$ is locally factorial, its reduced boundary $(\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr U)_\mathrm{red}$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $\mathscr X$.
head: environment
name: Purity of the boundary

title: Proof
body_md:
We first verify the assertions on density. If $\mathscr X$ is irreducible, then $\mathscr U \neq \varnothing$ as $\pi|_{\mathscr U}$ is surjective, and hence is dense. If $\mathscr X$ is normal, its irreducible components are open and closed. Moreover, preservation of $\pi$ gives an isomorphism $\Gamma(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \Gamma(\mathscr U,\mathcal O_{\mathscr U})$ since both sides are canonically identified with $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $\mathscr U$ missed an irreducible component $\mathscr X^\circ$ of $\mathscr X$, the non-zero idempotent equal to $1$ on $\mathscr X^\circ$ and $0$ on its complement would restrict to $0$ on $\mathscr U$, a contradiction. Thus $\mathscr U$ meets every irreducible component of $\mathscr X$ and is dense.

The open immersion $j$ is affine by \Cref{lem:affine-open}.  On a locally noetherian atlas, it becomes a dense affine open immersion of schemes, so each irreducible component of the complement has codimension $1$ \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BCU}{Tag 0BCU}]{stacks-project}. Codimension can be checked on an atlas, so the same holds for $\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr U$. If $\mathscr X$ is locally factorial, the Weil divisor $(\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr U)_\mathrm{red}$ is Cartier.
head: environment

label: thm:adequate-boundary
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $j: \mathscr U:=\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr D \hookrightarrow \mathscr X$ be the inclusion of the open complement of $\mathscr D$. First we claim that $j$ is affine. Indeed, affineness can be checked smooth local on the target $\mathscr X$, so this reduces to the scheme case \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07ZU}{Tag 07ZU}]{stacks-project}, as smooth pullback preserves effective Cartier divisors. 

(i) $\Leftrightarrow$ (ii). Since $j$ is affine, the composition $\pi \circ j$ is adequately affine \cite[Prop. 4.2.1 (2) and (1)]{AlperAdequate}. Therefore, the restriction $\pi|_{\mathscr U}=\pi \circ j: \mathscr U \to X$ is an adequate moduli space if and only if the canonical map $\mathcal O_X \to (\pi \circ j)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr U}$ is an isomorphism. To compute $(\pi \circ j)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr U}$, we note that
\[
j_* \mathcal O_{\mathscr U} = \varinjlim_{n \geq 0} \mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D).
\]
Indeed, this can be checked smooth locally on the target $\mathscr X$, on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec} A$ where $\mathscr D$ is defined by a single non-zero-divisor $f$. On such a chart,
\[
A_f = \varinjlim \left( A \xrightarrow{\cdot f} A \xrightarrow{\cdot f} A \to \cdots \right) = \bigcup_{n \geq 0} f^{-n}A,
\]
as every element of $A_f$ belongs to $f^{-n}A$ for some integer $n \geq 0$. Pushforward along a qcqs morphism commutes with filtered colimits of quasi-coherent modules, so
\[
(\pi \circ j)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr U} = \pi_* \left(j_* \mathcal O_{\mathscr U} \right) = \pi_*\varinjlim_{n \geq 0} \mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D) = \varinjlim_{n \geq 0} \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D) = \bigcup_{n \geq 0} \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D)
\]
The last equality holds because the transition maps $\pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D) \hookrightarrow \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}((n+1)\mathscr D)$ are injective. In particular, every $\pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D)$ embeds into this colimit. For every integer $n \geq 0$, the canonical map $\mathcal O_X \to (\pi \circ j)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr U}$ factors as
\[
\mathcal O_X \xrightarrow{\sim} \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X} \hookrightarrow \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D) \hookrightarrow \bigcup_{n \geq 0} \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D) = (\pi \circ j)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr U}.
\]
Consequently, if $\mathcal O_X \to (\pi \circ j)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr U}$ is an isomorphism, then every $\mathcal O_X \to \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D)$ is an isomorphism. Conversely, if every canonical map $\mathcal O_X \to \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D)$ is an isomorphism, their colimit is also $\mathcal O_X$. This proves the equivalence (i) $\Leftrightarrow$ (ii).

(iii) $\Rightarrow$ (ii). For every integer $n>0$ there is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_\mathscr X$-modules
\[
0 \to \mathcal O_\mathscr X((n-1)\mathscr D) \xrightarrow{\cdot s} \mathcal O_\mathscr X(n\mathscr D) \to i_*\mathcal N^{\otimes n} \to 0,
\]
where $s$ is the canonical section of $\mathcal O_\mathscr X(\mathscr D)$. Applying $\pi_*$ gives
\[
0 \to \pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X((n-1)\mathscr D) \to \pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X(n\mathscr D) \to (\pi \circ i)_*\mathcal N^{\otimes n}.
\]
Under (iii), the first map is an isomorphism. Induction, starting from $\mathcal O_X \xrightarrow{\sim} \pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X$, proves (ii).

(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (iii). The idea is that adequateness will imply that every local section of
$(\pi \circ i)_*\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$ has a positive tensor power equal to zero. Reducedness will then force the section itself to vanish. Consider the graded quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$-algebras
\[
\mathcal B:=\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} \mathcal O_\mathscr X(n\mathscr D) \text{ and } \mathcal Q:=\mathcal B/(s),
\]
where $s$ is regarded as a degree $1$ element. The degree $0$ part of the ideal $(s)$ is zero and degree $n>0$
part is $s\mathcal O_\mathscr X((n-1)\mathscr D)$. Consequently,
\[
\mathcal Q_0 = \mathcal O_{\mathscr X} \text{ and } \mathcal Q_n = \mathcal O_\mathscr X(n\mathscr D)/s\mathcal O_\mathscr X((n-1)\mathscr D) \text{ for } n>0.
\]
The short exact sequence above gives
$\mathcal Q_n \simeq i_*\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$ for every $n>0$, and these identifications are compatible with multiplication in positive degrees. In particular, the power $h^r$ of a homogeneous section of degree $n>0$ corresponds to its tensor power $h^{\otimes r}$ as a section of $\mathcal N^{\otimes nr}$.

By (ii), together with $\mathcal O_X \xrightarrow{\sim} \pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X$ for $n=0$, the canonical maps $\mathcal O_X \to \pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X(n\mathscr D)$ sending $a \mapsto (\pi^*a)s^n$ are isomorphisms for all $n \geq 0$. Since $\pi$ is qcqs, its pushforward on quasi-coherent modules commutes with direct sums. This gives an isomorphism $\mathcal O_X[s] \xrightarrow{\sim} \pi_*\mathcal B$ of graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebras. In particular, every degree $n$ local section of $\pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X(n\mathscr D)$ is a multiple of $s^n$.

Let us fix an integer $n>0$. For any affine \'{e}tale chart $W \to X$ and section $h$ of $(\pi \circ i)_*\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$ over $W$, under the identification $(\pi \circ i)_*\mathcal N^{\otimes n} \simeq \pi_*\mathcal Q_n$, one may view $h$ as a section of $\pi_*\mathcal Q$ over $W$. Since $\pi$ is adequately affine, for the quotient of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_\mathscr X$-algebras $\mathcal B \twoheadrightarrow \mathcal Q$ and the section $h$ of $\pi_*\mathcal Q$, after an \'{e}tale refinement of $W$ if necessary, some positive power $h^r$ lifts to $\pi_*\mathcal B$. The quotient map preserves the grading, and $h^r$ is homogeneous of degree $nr$. Taking the degree $nr$ component gives a lift of $h^r$ in $\pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X(nr\mathscr D)$. But every such lift is a multiple of $s^{nr}$, whose image in $\mathcal Q$ is zero. This shows that $h^r=0$, hence $h^{\otimes r}=0$.

Since $W \to X$ is \'{e}tale and $\mathscr D$ is reduced, $\mathscr D \times_X W$ is reduced. On a reduced stack, a section of a line bundle whose positive tensor power is zero is itself zero, as is checked by trivializing the line bundle on a reduced atlas. Thus $h=0$ \'{e}tale locally on $W$, and hence on $W$.

label: ex:adequate-not-good
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:adequate-not-good}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ and let
${\mathbb{G}_m} \times \operatorname{SL}_2$ act on $\mathbb A^1$ by $(a,h).x=ax$. There is an adequate moduli space $[\mathbb A^1/({\mathbb{G}_m} \times \operatorname{SL}_2)] \to \operatorname{Spec} k$. Removing the zero divisor gives $\mathrm{BSL}_2$ with the same
adequate moduli space. This follows directly from computing the invariant rings, or from \Cref{thm:adequate-boundary}: each positive power
of the normal bundle has a non-zero ${\mathbb{G}_m}$-character.

label: cor:removable-restriction
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:removable-restriction}
Let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space. If $\mathscr D' \subseteq \mathscr D$ are effective Cartier divisors on $\mathscr X$ and $\mathscr D$ is removable for $\pi$, then $\mathscr D'$ is removable for $\pi$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For every integer $n > 0$, we have canonical inclusions $\mathcal O_X \hookrightarrow \pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X(n\mathscr D') \hookrightarrow \pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X(n\mathscr D)$. The composition is an isomorphism by \Cref{thm:adequate-boundary}, so the first map is also an isomorphism. Then applying \Cref{thm:adequate-boundary} to $\mathscr D'$ proves the result.
head: environment

label: prop:descent-obstruction
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:descent-obstruction}
Let $\mathscr X$ be an algebraic stack admitting an adequate moduli space $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$. Let $\varnothing \neq \mathscr D \subseteq \mathscr X$ be an effective Cartier divisor. If $\mathcal O_\mathscr X(n\mathscr D) \simeq \pi^*A$ for some $n>0$ and $A \in \operatorname{Pic}(X)$, then $\mathscr D$ is not removable for $\pi$.
head: environment
name: Descent obstruction

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathscr U:=\mathscr X\setminus\mathscr D$, and let
$s\in\Gamma(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_\mathscr X(\mathscr D))$ be the canonical section defining
$\mathscr D$. We conclude by showing that $\pi|_{\mathscr U}: \mathscr U \to X$ is not surjective. Fix an isomorphism
$\mathcal O_\mathscr X(n\mathscr D) \simeq \pi^*A$ and use it to regard
$s^{\otimes n}$ as a section of $\pi^*A$. Since $\pi$ is an adequate moduli space, the projection formula for $A$ gives canonical isomorphisms $A \xrightarrow{\sim} A \otimes_{\mathcal O_X} \pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X \xrightarrow{\sim} \pi_*\pi^*A$. So there is a unique section $t \in \Gamma(X,A)$
whose pullback is $s^{\otimes n}$. Let $Z(t) \subseteq X$ be its zero locus. Since zero loci of sections of line bundles commute with base change, we have an equality of closed substacks $\mathscr X \times_X Z(t) = Z(\pi^*t) = Z(s^{\otimes n}) = n\mathscr D$. As $|n\mathscr D|=|\mathscr D| \neq \varnothing$, this implies that
$Z(t) \neq \varnothing$. Taking complements gives $\mathscr U=\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr D = \mathscr X \times_X (X \setminus Z(t))$. Thus $\pi|_\mathscr U$ factors through the open subspace
$X \setminus Z(t) \subsetneq X$ and is not surjective.

label: thm:divisorial-classification
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:divisorial-classification}
Let $\mathscr X$ be a locally factorial algebraic stack with affine diagonal, and let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space. Taking complements gives a bijection from reduced effective Cartier divisors $\mathscr D$ on $\mathscr X$ satisfying
\[
(\pi \circ i)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr D}(n\mathscr D)=0 \text{ for every integer } n>0
\]
to $\operatorname{Op}(\pi)$, where $i: \mathscr D \hookrightarrow \mathscr X$ is the closed immersion.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\Cref{thm:adequate-boundary} shows that taking complements sends every reduced effective Cartier divisor satisfying the vanishing condition to an open substack preserving $\pi$. This assignment is injective because a reduced closed substack is determined by its complement. Conversely, let $\mathscr U \subsetneq \mathscr X$ be an open substack preserving $\pi$. Then $\mathscr D=(\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr U)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is an effective Cartier divisor by \Cref{lem:boundary-purity}. Applying \Cref{thm:adequate-boundary} to $\mathscr D$ gives
$(\pi \circ i)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr D}(n\mathscr D)=0$ for every $n>0$. This shows the surjectivity.
head: environment

label: cor:simplicial-correspondence
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:simplicial-correspondence}
Let $\mathscr X$ be a noetherian locally factorial algebraic stack with affine
diagonal, and let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space. For a finite subset $\sigma \subseteq \mathrm{PD}(\pi)$, write
\[
\mathscr D_\sigma:=\sum_{\mathscr D \in \sigma} \mathscr D \text{ and } i_\sigma: \mathscr D_\sigma \hookrightarrow \mathscr X.
\]
Let
\[
\mathcal K(\pi):=\left\{ \sigma \subseteq \mathrm{PD}(\pi) \text{ finite}: (\pi \circ i_\sigma)_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr D_\sigma}(n\mathscr D_\sigma)=0 \text{ for every } n>0\right\}.
\]
Then $\mathcal K(\pi)$ is an abstract simplicial complex with vertex set $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)$, and a finite collection of vertices forms a face precisely when the complement of their union preserves $\pi$. The assignment $\sigma \mapsto \mathscr X \setminus \mathscr D_\sigma$ is an order-reversing bijection from its faces to $\operatorname{Op}(\pi)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Local factoriality ensures that every prime divisor on $\mathscr X$ is Cartier
and that a finite sum of distinct prime divisors is reduced.

The empty set belongs to $\mathcal K(\pi)$, and every singleton
$\{\mathscr D\}$ with $\mathscr D \in \mathrm{PD}(\pi)$ belongs to $\mathcal K(\pi)$ by
\Cref{thm:adequate-boundary}. If $\sigma \in \mathcal K(\pi)$ and $\tau \subseteq \sigma$, then $\mathscr U_\sigma$ preserves
$\pi$ and $\mathscr D_\tau \leq \mathscr D_\sigma$. \Cref{cor:removable-restriction} shows that $\mathscr U_\tau$ preserves $\pi$. Since $\mathscr D_\tau$ is reduced, \Cref{thm:adequate-boundary} gives $\tau \in\mathcal K(\pi)$.
Thus $\mathcal K(\pi)$ is an abstract simplicial complex with the vertex set $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)$.

By \Cref{thm:adequate-boundary}, every face $\sigma$ gives an open substack $\mathscr U_\sigma$ preserving $\pi$. Conversely, let $\mathscr U \subseteq \mathscr X$ be an open substack preserving $\pi$. The reduced complement $\mathscr D:=(\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr U)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is an effective Cartier divisor by \Cref{lem:boundary-purity}. Since $\mathscr X$ is noetherian, $\mathscr D$ has finitely many prime
components. Let $\sigma$ be their set. Applying \Cref{cor:removable-restriction} to each prime component of $\mathscr D$
shows that $\sigma \subseteq \mathrm{PD}(\pi)$, and $\mathscr D=\mathscr D_\sigma$. Another application of \Cref{thm:adequate-boundary} gives $\sigma \in \mathcal K(\pi)$, with $\mathscr U=\mathscr U_\sigma$.

label: setup:quotient
title: Setup
body_md:
\label{setup:quotient}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $G$ be a reductive group over $k$, and let $X$ be a $k$-variety with a $G$-action. Suppose that $X$ admits a good quotient $q: X \to X/G$.
head: environment

label: lem:quotient-images
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:quotient-images}
Assume the hypotheses of  \Cref{setup:quotient}. For every cocharacter $\lambda \in X_*(G)$ and every connected component $F \in \pi_0(X_\lambda)$, the subset $G.C_{\lambda,F} \subseteq X$ is closed, and there are only finitely many distinct subsets of the form $G.C_{\lambda,F}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\lambda \in X_*(G)$ and $F \in \pi_0(X_\lambda)$. Since $X$ admits a good quotient, by \Cref{rmk:ev1-closed-immersion} we identify $C_{\lambda,F} \subseteq X_\lambda^+$ as a closed subscheme of $X$ via the closed immersion $\operatorname{ev}_1: X_\lambda^+ \hookrightarrow X$. 

For the closedness. The parabolic subgroup $P_\lambda^+ \subseteq G$ preserves $C_{\lambda,F}$. Consider the morphism
\[
\iota: G \times^{P^+_\lambda} C_{\lambda,F} \to G/P^+_\lambda \times X \text{ sending } [(g,x)] \mapsto (gP^+_\lambda,g.x). 
\]
This is a closed immersion. Indeed, after the faithfully flat base change $G \to G/P^+_\lambda$, it becomes $G \times C_{\lambda,F} \to G \times X$ sending $(g,x) \to (g,g.x)$, which is the closed immersion $\operatorname{id}_G \times \operatorname{ev}_1: G \times C_{\lambda,F} \hookrightarrow G \times X$ followed by an automorphism of $G \times X$. Since $G/P_\lambda^+$ is projective, the composition 
\[
G \times^{P^+_\lambda} C_{\lambda,F} \xrightarrow{\iota} G/P^+_\lambda \times X \xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2} X
\]
is projective with set-theoretical image $G.C_{\lambda,F}$. This proves the closedness. 

For the finiteness. Fix a maximal torus $\mathbb T \subseteq G$. If $\mu=g\lambda g^{-1}$ for some $g\in G(k)$, then multiplication by $g$ induces isomorphisms $X_\lambda^+ \xrightarrow{\sim} X_\mu^+$ and $X_\lambda \xrightarrow{\sim} X_\mu$ compatible with evaluation maps, i.e., $g.C_{\lambda,F}=C_{\mu,gF}$. Thus we have $G.C_{\lambda,F}=G.C_{\mu,gF}$. Since every cocharacter of $G$ is conjugate to a cocharacter of $\mathbb T$, for the finiteness it suffices to consider $\lambda \in X_*(\mathbb T)$.

Suppose first that $X=\operatorname{Spec} A$ is affine. Choose homogeneous generators $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ of $A$ as a $k$-algebra, with weights $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_n \in X^*(\mathbb T)$. Then by \cite[\S 1.3.4]{Drinfeld}
\[
X_\lambda^+ = \operatorname{Spec} A/I_\lambda^- \text{ with } I_\lambda^-:=
\langle f_i: \langle \lambda,\chi_i \rangle < 0 \rangle.
\]
This shows that there are finitely many distinct $X_\lambda^+$. Each $X_\lambda^+$ has finitely many connected components, so only finitely many subsets $C_{\lambda,F}$ occur.

For general $X$, by \cite[Thm. 4.1]{Luna-slice-for-stacks} and quasi-compactness of $X$, there exists a $\mathbb T$-equivariant \'{e}tale surjection $f: Y \twoheadrightarrow X$ with $Y$ affine. By the affine case, the collection $\mathscr D:=\{Z \in \pi_0(Y_\mu^+): \mu \in X_*(\mathbb T)\}$ of subsets of $Y$ is finite. The induced morphism $f_\lambda^+=f|_{Y_\lambda^+}: Y_\lambda^+ \twoheadrightarrow X_\lambda^+$ is surjective by \cite[Prop. 5.20]{Luna-slice-for-stacks}. Hence
\[
C_{\lambda,F} = \bigcup_{Z \in \pi_0(Y_\lambda^+), f(Z) \subseteq C_{\lambda,F}} f(Z).
\]
Thus $C_{\lambda,F}$ is a union of images of elements in the finite collection $\mathscr D$ under the fixed $f$. This proves the finiteness. The finiteness part does not need the existence of a good quotient.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\mathcal L$ be a $G$-linearized line bundle on $X$. For any cocharacter $\lambda: {\mathbb{G}_m} \to G$ and any connected subset $F \subseteq X_\lambda$, we define 
\[
\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal L|_F):=\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal L|_x) \in \mathbb Z \text{ for some } x \in F.
\]
This is well-defined: the $\lambda$-weight, being discrete, is locally constant on $X_\lambda$, hence constant on the connected subset $F$. So the value of $\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal L|_F)$ does not depend on the choice of $x \in F$.

For a line bundle $\mathcal L$ on $\Theta:=[\mathbb A^1/{\mathbb{G}_m}]$, we define $\operatorname{wt}(\mathcal L):=\operatorname{wt}_{\mathbb{G}_m}(\mathcal L|_0) \in \mathbb Z$. For any point $x \in C_{\lambda,F}$, its complete $\lambda$-orbit $\lambda_x: \mathbb A^1 \to X$ satisfies $\lambda_x(1)=x$ and $x_0:=\lambda_x(0)=\lim_{t \to 0} \lambda(t).x \in F$. This defines a morphism $\lambda_x: \Theta=[\mathbb A^1/{\mathbb{G}_m}] \to [X/G]$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:comparing-weight}
\operatorname{wt}(\lambda_x^*\mathcal L) = \operatorname{wt}_{\mathbb{G}_m}(\lambda_x^*\mathcal L|_0) = \operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal L|_{x_0}) = \operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal L|_F).   
\end{equation}

title: Proof
body_md: Since $\Gamma(\Theta,f^*\mathcal L)=0$ by \Cref{lem:theta-weight}, for the canonical section $s$ of $\mathcal L$ this means $f^*s=0$. Then $f$ factors through the zero locus of $s$, which is $\mathscr D$.

label: cor:weight-inclusion
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For (i), suppose $\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal L|_F)<0$. By $G$-invariance it suffices to show $C_{\lambda,F} \subseteq D$. For any $x \in C_{\lambda,F}$, let $\lambda_x: \mathbb A^1 \to X$ be its complete $\lambda$-orbit map so $\lambda_x(1)=x$ and $\lambda_x(0) \in F$, and it induces $\lambda_x: [\mathbb A^1/{\mathbb{G}_m}] \to [X/G]$. If $\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal L|_F)<0$, then $\operatorname{wt}(\lambda_x^*\mathcal L)<0$ by \eqref{eq:comparing-weight}. This shows that $\lambda_x(1)=x \in D$ by \Cref{cor:negative-in-D}. For (ii), let $s \in \Gamma(X,\mathcal L)^G$ be the canonical section of $\mathcal L$ defining $D$. Since $D \cap F=\varnothing$, the section $s$ is nowhere vanishing on $F$. So it induces a $\lambda$-equivariant trivialization $\mathcal O_F \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal L|_F$ sending $1 \mapsto s|_F$. Since $\lambda$ acts trivially on $F$, it follows that $\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal L|_F)=0$.

label: thm:quotient-boundary
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $X$ admits a good quotient, each subset $G.C_{\lambda,F}$ is closed in $X$, and they form a finite collection by \Cref{lem:quotient-images}. To show the equivalence we introduce a bridge condition

\vspace{0.3em}

(\S) for every geometric point $x$ of $D$, there exists a morphism $f: \Theta \to [D/G]$ with $f(1) \simeq x$ and $\operatorname{wt}(f^*\mathcal N)<0$, where $\mathcal N:=\mathcal N_{D/X}=\mathcal L|_D$ is the normal line bundle.

\vspace{0.3em}

Fix an \'{e}tale cover $W \to X/G$ with $W$ affine. Since $\pi$ is affine and $W$ is affine, its base change $X_W:=X\times_{X/G}W$ is affine. The following chain proves the equivalence
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
\text{the Cartier divisor } D \subseteq X \text{ is removable for } \pi \ar[d,"\text{by \Cref{thm:adequate-boundary}}"] \\
\Gamma(D_W,N_W^{\otimes n})^G=0 \text{ for every } n>0 \ar[u] \ar[d,"D_W \text{ is reduced}"] \\
D_W^\mathrm{ss}(N_W) = \varnothing \ar[d,"\text{by Hilbert-Mumford criterion}"] \ar[u] \\
(\S) \text{ on } D_W \ar[u] \ar[d,"\text{by \Cref{lem:lifting-Theta}}"] \\
(\S) \ar[u],
\end{tikzcd}
\]
where
\[
D_W:=D \times_{X/G} W \text{ and } N_W:=p_D^*\mathcal N \simeq \mathcal N_{D_W/X_W} \text{ with } p_D:D_W \to D \text{ the projection}
\]
The $G$-action on $D_W$ and the $G$-linearization of $N_W$ are induced by pullback, with $G$ acting trivially on $W$.


Suppose the condition (\S) holds. Then each geometric point of $D$ belongs to some $C_{\lambda,F}$ such that $\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal L|_F)<0$, so \Cref{cor:weight-inclusion} gives \eqref{eq:character-D}. Conversely, suppose the equality \eqref{eq:character-D} holds. Then each geometric point $x$ of $D$ can be written as $x=g.y$ for some $g \in G$ and $y \in C_{\lambda,F}$ such that $\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal L|_F)<0$. The cocharacter $g \lambda g^{-1}$ has a limit at $x$, lying in $gF \subseteq D$, with the same negative weight. This defines a morphism $f: \Theta \to [D/G]$ with $f(1) \simeq x$ and $\operatorname{wt}(f^*\mathcal N)<0$. This proves (\S).

label: cor:finite-reductive
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:finite-reductive}
Assume the hypotheses of  \Cref{setup:quotient}. Assume in addition that $X$ is smooth. Then $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)$ is finite, and each element of $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)$ is of the form
\[
G.C_{\lambda,F} \text{ for some } \lambda \in X_*(G), F \in \pi_0(X_{\lambda}) \text{ with } \operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal O_X(G.C_{\lambda,F})|_F)<0.
\]
Write $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)=\{D_1,\ldots,D_r\}$. For a subset $\sigma \subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}$, write 
\[
D_\sigma:=\sum_{i \in \sigma} D_i \text{ and } \mathcal L_\sigma:=\mathcal O_X(D_\sigma).
\]
Call $\sigma$ \emph{admissible} if, for every $i \in \sigma$, there exist $\lambda_i \in X_*(G)$ and $F_i \in \pi_0(X_{\lambda_i})$ such that
\[
D_i=G.C_{\lambda_i,F_i}  \text{ and } \operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{F_i})<0.
\]
The assignment $\sigma \mapsto X \setminus D_\sigma$ is an order-reversing bijection from admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,r\}$ to $\operatorname{Op}(q)$. In particular, we have $|\operatorname{Op}(q)| \leq 2^r$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By definition, every element of $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)$ is removable and prime, hence of the form $G.C_{\lambda,F}$ for a single $\lambda \in X_*(G)$ and $F \in \pi_0(X_\lambda)$ with $\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal O_X(G.C_{\lambda,F})|_F)<0$ by \Cref{thm:quotient-boundary}. Such closed subsets $G.C_{\lambda,F}$ form a finite collection by \Cref{lem:quotient-images}. 

For every admissible subset $\sigma \subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}$, the closed subscheme $D_\sigma$ is reduced and removable for $\pi$ by \Cref{thm:quotient-boundary}. This means the assignment $\sigma \mapsto X \setminus D_\sigma$ is well-defined and it is injective. Conversely, let $D = D_1 + \cdots + D_s$ be a reduced removable closed subscheme of $X$. Then $D$ is a $G$-invariant effective Cartier divisor on $X$ by \Cref{lem:boundary-purity}. Each prime boundary $D_i$ is $G$-invariant since $G$ is connected, and is removable for $\pi$ by \Cref{cor:removable-restriction}. Then $D_i \in \mathrm{PD}(\pi)$. 

Since $X$ is smooth, each connected attractor $C_{\lambda,F}$ is smooth by \cite[Prop. 1.4.20]{Drinfeld}, hence irreducible. As $G$ is connected, the $G$-saturation $G.C_{\lambda,F}$ is also irreducible. By \Cref{thm:quotient-boundary} and \Cref{lem:quotient-images}, $D$ is a finite union of these
closed irreducible subsets with $\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda}(\mathcal O_X(D)|_F)<0$. Every prime component $D_i$ therefore equals one of the subsets occurring in this union, giving the required weight condition.

Counting possible subsets gives the upper bound.
head: environment

label: rmk:weight-computation-torus
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk:weight-computation-torus}
Fix a subset $\sigma \subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}$. For any fixed index $i \in \sigma$, by \Cref{cor:finite-reductive}, there exist $\lambda_i \in X_*(G)$ and $F_i \in \pi_0(X_{\lambda_i})$ such that
\[
D_i=G.C_{\lambda_i,F_i} \text{ and } \operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal O_X(D_i)|_{F_i})<0.
\]
Then we can compute
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{F_i})&=\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal O_X(D_\sigma)|_{F_i})=\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}\left(\mathcal O_X\left(\sum_{j \in \sigma} D_j\right)|_{F_i}\right) \\
&=\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}\left(\bigotimes_{j \in \sigma} \mathcal O_X(D_j)|_{F_i}\right) = \sum_{j \in \sigma} \operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal O_X(D_j)|_{F_i}) \\
&=\underbrace{\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal O_X(D_i)|_{F_i})}_{<0 \text{ by } \ref{thm:quotient-boundary}}+\sum_{j \in \sigma \setminus \{i\}} \underbrace{\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal O_X(D_j)|_{F_i})}_{\geq 0 \text{ by } \ref{cor:weight-inclusion}}
\end{align*}
In particular, if $\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{F_i})<0$ then $\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal O_X(D_i)|_{F_i})<0$. This explains \Cref{cor:removable-restriction} from the weight perspective. By \Cref{cor:finite-reductive}, we see $D_\sigma$ is removable if and only if for each $i \in \sigma$ the pair $(\lambda_i,F_i)$ can be arranged so that the $|\sigma|$-dimensional vector
\[
(\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{F_i}))_{i \in \sigma} \in \mathbb Z^{|\sigma|}
\]
consists of negative components, if and only if the $|\sigma| \times |\sigma|$ matrix
\[
\left(\operatorname{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal O_X(D_j)|_{F_i})\right)_{i,j \in \sigma} \in \operatorname{Mat}_{|\sigma|}(\mathbb Z)
\]
is a row strictly diagonally dominant (SDD) matrix.

label: ex:determinant
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:determinant}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $G:=\operatorname{SL}_2$ act
on $X:=\operatorname{Mat}_2$ by left multiplication. By the first fundamental theorem of invariant theory for $\operatorname{SL}_2$ (see, e.g., \cite[\S 3]{MR979587}, or \cite[Thm. 3.2]{MR485944}, or \cite[Thm. 3.1]{MR422314}) we have $k[X]^G=k[\det]$. Thus, taking determinants defines a good quotient $\pi=\det: X \to \mathbb A^1$. Consider the cocharacter $\lambda: {\mathbb{G}_m} \to G$ sending $t \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1})$. We compute
\[
F = X_\lambda = \left\{
\begin{pmatrix}
0 & 0 \\
0 & 0
\end{pmatrix}
\right\} \text{ and } C_{\lambda,F} = \left\{
\begin{pmatrix}
a & b \\
0 & 0
\end{pmatrix}: a,b \in k
\right\}.
\]
Its $G$-saturation is the locus of rank $\leq 1$ matrices $D:=G.C_{\lambda,F} = \mathbf{V}(\det)$. This is a reduced prime effective Cartier divisor on $X$, but not removable for $\pi$. Indeed, since the determinant function $\det$ is $G$-invariant, we have
\[
\operatorname{wt}_\mu(\mathcal O_X(D)|_E) = \operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal O_X(D)|_F)=0
\]
for any $\mu \in X_*(G)$ and $E \in \pi_0(X_\mu)$ with $D=G.C_{\mu,E}$, as every non-trivial cocharacter of $\operatorname{SL}_2$ is conjugate to a positive multiple of $\lambda$, and every corresponding $G$-saturation is $D$. The negative-weight condition in \Cref{thm:quotient-boundary} fails.

The non-removability of $D$ can also be seen directly: removing $D$ gives the good quotient
\[
\pi=\det: X \setminus D \simeq \operatorname{GL}_2 \to {\mathbb{G}_m}.
\]

label: lem:torus-cell
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:torus-cell}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $\mathbb T$ be a torus over $k$, and let $X$ be a smooth $k$-variety with a $\mathbb T$-action. Suppose that $X$ admits a good quotient $q: X \to X/\mathbb T$. Let $\lambda \in X_*(\mathbb T)$ and $F \in \pi_0(X_\lambda)$. If $C_{\lambda,F}$ has codimension one in $X$, then it is a $\mathbb T$-invariant smooth prime Cartier divisor on $X$ and $\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal O_X(C_{\lambda,F})|_F)<0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The fixed and attracting loci of a smooth scheme are smooth \cite[Prop. 1.4.20]{Drinfeld}. Then the codimension-one connected component $C_{\lambda,F}$ is a smooth prime Cartier divisor on $X$. Choose a $\lambda$-fixed point $x \in F$. The tangent spaces at $x$ satisfy \cite[Prop. 1.4.11 (vi)]{Drinfeld}
\[
\mathrm T_xC_{\lambda,F}=(\mathrm T_xX)_{\lambda,\geq 0}.
\]
The fiber of the normal line bundle $\mathcal O_X(C_{\lambda,F})|_{C_{\lambda,F}}$ at $x$ is the quotient $\mathrm T_xX/(\mathrm T_xX)_{\lambda,\geq 0}$, which is one-dimensional and has negative $\lambda$-weight. This finishes the proof.

label: thm:main-Gm
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For any subset $\sigma \subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}$, define $\sigma^\pm:=\sigma \cap \mathrm{PD}^\pm \subseteq \mathrm{PD}^\pm$. By \Cref{cor:finite-reductive}, we have a bijection
\[
\left\{
\sigma \subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}: \operatorname{wt}_{\pm\operatorname{id}}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{X_i})<0 \text{ for } i \in \sigma^\pm
\right\}
\leftrightarrow 
\left\{
{\mathbb{G}_m}\text{-invariant opens of } X \text{ preserving } \pi
\right\}.
\]
It remains to show the weight condition on the left-hand side is equivalent to $\sigma^+ \cap \sigma^- = \varnothing$. Indeed, for each $i \in \mathrm{PD}^+ \cup \mathrm{PD}^-$, write
\[
\operatorname{wt}_{\pm \operatorname{id}}(\mathcal O_X(X_i^+)|_{X_i})=\mp a_i \text{ and } \operatorname{wt}_{\pm \operatorname{id}}(\mathcal O_X(X_i^-)|_{X_i})=\pm b_i,
\]
for some integers $a_i, b_i>0$. For $j \neq i$, the fixed component $X_i$
is disjoint from $X_j^\pm$. Hence, by \Cref{cor:weight-inclusion},
\[
\operatorname{wt}_{\pm \operatorname{id}}(\mathcal O_X(X_j^\pm)|_{X_i}) = 0.
\]
Therefore, by \Cref{rmk:weight-computation-torus}, for each $i \in \sigma = \sigma^+ \cup \sigma^-$ we have
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{wt}_{\pm \operatorname{id}}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{X_i})&=\sum_{j \in \sigma^+}\operatorname{wt}_{\pm \operatorname{id}}(\mathcal O_X(X_j^+)|_{X_i}) + \sum_{j \in \sigma^-} \operatorname{wt}_{\pm \operatorname{id}}(\mathcal O_X(X_j^-)|_{X_i}) \\
&=\mp \mathbf{1}_{\sigma^+}(i) \cdot a_i \pm \mathbf{1}_{\sigma^-}(i) \cdot b_i.
\end{align*}
If $\sigma^+ \cap \sigma^- = \varnothing$, then
\[
\operatorname{wt}_{\operatorname{id}}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{X_i})=-a_i<0 \text{ for every } i \in \sigma^+,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{wt}_{-\operatorname{id}}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{X_i})=-b_i<0 \text{ for every } i \in \sigma^-.
\]
Conversely, if $i \in \sigma^+ \cap \sigma^-$, the two required
inequalities are
\[
\operatorname{wt}_{\operatorname{id}}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{X_i})=-a_i+b_i<0 \text{ and } \operatorname{wt}_{-\operatorname{id}}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{X_i})=a_i-b_i<0,
\]
and they cannot hold simultaneously. Thus the weight inequalities $\operatorname{wt}_{\pm \operatorname{id}}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{X_i})<0$ hold for $i \in \sigma^\pm$ if and only if $\sigma^+ \cap \sigma^-=\varnothing$.

label: ex:axes
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:axes}
Let $\mathbb T:=\mathbb{G}_m^r$ act on $\mathbb A^{2r}$ by $(t_i)_i.(x_i,y_i)_i=(t_ix_i,t_i^{-1}y_i)_i$. The good quotient is $q: \mathbb A^{2r} \to \mathbb A^r$ sending $(x_i,y_i)_i \mapsto (x_iy_i)_i$. For each $i$, let $\lambda_i: {\mathbb{G}_m} \to \mathbb T$ be the $i$-th coordinate cocharacter. Both $\pm \lambda_i$ have fixed locus $F_i=\mathbf{V}(x_i,y_i)$, and
\[
D_i^+:=G.C_{\lambda_i,F_i}=\mathbf{V}(y_i) \text{ and } D_i^-:=G.C_{-\lambda_i,F_i}=\mathbf{V}(x_i).
\]
A cocharacter with $s$ non-zero coordinates has attracting locus of codimension $s$, so these are the only divisorial attracting images. Ordering the signs as $+,-$, the weight matrix is
\[
\left(
\operatorname{wt}_{\varepsilon\lambda_i}
\bigl(\mathcal O_X(D_j^\delta)|_{F_i}\bigr)
\right)_{(i,\varepsilon),(j,\delta)}
=
\mathbb{I}_r \otimes
\begin{pmatrix}
-1 & 1 \\
1 & -1
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
By \Cref{thm:quotient-boundary} and \Cref{cor:finite-reductive}, $\mathrm{PD}(q)=\{D_i^\pm: 1 \leq i \leq r\}$, and the preserving opens are exactly the complements of unions
containing at most one divisor from each pair $(D_i^+,D_i^-)$. Thus $|\mathrm{PD}(q)|=2r$ and $|\operatorname{Op}(q)|=3^r$.

label: cor:affine-space-three-opens
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:affine-space-three-opens}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let ${\mathbb{G}_m}$ act on the affine space $X:=\mathbb A^n$ and let $q: X \to X/{\mathbb{G}_m}$ be the good quotient. Then $|\operatorname{Op}(q)| \leq 3$. The upper bound is sharp for every $n \geq 2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first show the fixed locus $X^{\mathbb{G}_m}$ is non-empty and connected. If the ${\mathbb{G}_m}$-action on $\mathbb A^n$ is linear, this can be seen directly using coordinates. In general, choose a ${\mathbb{G}_m}$-equivariant closed immersion $X \hookrightarrow V$ into a finite-dimensional ${\mathbb{G}_m}$-representation. Choose a prime $\ell \neq \mathrm{char}(k)$ larger than the absolute values of all non-zero ${\mathbb{G}_m}$-weights of $V$. Then $V^{\mu_\ell}=V^{\mathbb{G}_m}$ and hence $X^{\mu_\ell}=X^{\mathbb{G}_m}$. Since $\mu_\ell(k)$ is cyclic of order $\ell$, applying \cite[Cor. 4.3]{Symonds-Gm} to $X$ gives
\[
\sum_{i \geq 0} \dim_{\mathbb F_\ell} H_c^i(X^{\mathbb{G}_m},\mathbb F_\ell)=1,
\]
where $H_c^i$ denotes étale cohomology with compact supports. Each $Z \in \pi_0(X^{\mathbb{G}_m})$ contributes a non-zero group $H_c^{2\dim Z}(Z,\mathbb F_\ell)$. The equality therefore implies that $X^{\mathbb{G}_m} \neq \varnothing$ and has exactly one connected component. 

By \Cref{thm:main-Gm}, the preserving
opens are $X$, or $X\setminus X_{\operatorname{id}}^+$ if $\operatorname{codim}_X X_{\operatorname{id}}^+=1$, or $X\setminus X_{\operatorname{id}}^-$ if $\operatorname{codim}_X X_{\operatorname{id}}^-=1$. The two attracting divisors cannot be removed simultaneously. This proves the upper bound. Sharpness follows from \Cref{ex:axes}.

label: prop:chart-test
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose an open substack $\mathscr U \subseteq \mathscr X$ preserves $\pi$. Then $\mathscr U \hookrightarrow \mathscr X$ is affine by \Cref{lem:affine-open} and hence the composition $\mathscr U \hookrightarrow \mathscr X \to X$ is adequately affine. Consider the following Cartesian diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
W_i \ar[r,two heads] \ar[d,hook] & \left[ W_i/G_i \right] \ar[r] \ar[d,hook] & \mathscr U \ar[d,hook] \\
V_i \ar[r,two heads] & \left[ V_i/G_i \right] \ar[r] \ar[d,"\pi_i"',two heads] & \mathscr X \ar[d,"\pi",two heads] \\
& X_i \ar[r] & X
\end{tikzcd}
\]
The $G_i$-torsor $W_i \twoheadrightarrow [W_i/G_i]$ is affine as $G_i$ is affine, and $[W_i/G_i] \to X_i$ is an adequate moduli space as a flat base change of $\pi|_\mathscr U: \mathscr U \to X$. So the composition $W_i \to X_i$ is adequately affine, hence affine by \cite[Thm. 4.3.1]{AlperAdequate}. In particular, $W_i$ is affine. The condition that $[W_i/G_i] \to X_i$ is an adequate moduli space is precisely the isomorphism in \eqref{eq:chart-test}, using the isomorphism $\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal O_{X_i}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O_{V_i})^{G_i}$.

Conversely, since $W_i$ is affine, the morphism $[W_i/G_i] \to \operatorname{Spec} \Gamma(W_i,\mathcal O_{W_i})^{G_i}$ is an adequate moduli space \cite[Rmk. 9.1.5]{AlperAdequate}, and the isomorphism in \eqref{eq:chart-test} identifies that with $X_i$. So each open substack $[W_i/G_i] \subseteq [V_i/G_i]$ preserves $\pi_i$. This compatible family of open substacks $[W_i/G_i]$ descends uniquely along the \'{e}tale cover $\{[V_i/G_i] \to \mathscr X\}$ to an open substack $\mathscr U \subseteq \mathscr X$, whose pullbacks to each $V_i$ are the prescribed $W_i$. The open substack $\mathscr U \subseteq \mathscr X$ preserves $\pi$ as adequate moduli spaces descend along any fpqc cover \cite[Prop. 5.2.9 (2)]{AlperAdequate}.

label: def:locally-reductive
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:locally-reductive}
A quasi-separated algebraic stack $\mathscr X$ with affine stabilizers is called \emph{locally reductive} if every point of $\mathscr X$ specializes to a closed point and every closed point $x$ admits an \'etale quotient presentation, which is a pointed \'{e}tale morphism $([\operatorname{Spec} A/\operatorname{GL}_n],w) \to (\mathscr X,x)$ that induces an isomorphism of stabilizer groups at $w$.
head: environment
name: Local reductivity, , Defns. 2.1 and 2.5

title: Remark
body_md:
The technical condition ``local reductivity'' emerges due to the lack of a local structure theorem of algebraic stacks in positive characteristic. For an algebraic stack $\mathscr X$ of finite type over a field, with affine stabilizers and admitting an adequate moduli space, local reductivity is automatic in the following cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item 
The adequate moduli space of $\mathscr X$ is actually a good moduli space (e.g. if $\mathscr X$ is of characteristic $0$).
\item
The stack $\mathscr X$ admits a representable morphism to a quotient stack for an action of a reductive group. Indeed, this is covered in the proof of \cite[Prop. 3.28]{dario-zhang}.
\end{itemize}

title: Proof
body_md: For each closed point $z \in |\mathscr X|$, there is an \'{e}tale neighborhood $g_z: \operatorname{Spec} B_z \to X$ of $\pi(z)$ and a Cartesian diagram as above \cite[Prop. 2.10]{AHLH}. It remains to show the morphisms $g_z$ cover $X$. Let $x \in |X|$. Since $\pi$ is surjective, choose $\xi \in |\mathscr X|$ with $\pi(\xi)=x$. By local reductivity of $\mathscr X$, the point $\xi$ specializes to a closed point $z \in |\mathscr X|$, so $x$ specializes to $\pi(z)$. The image of $g_z$ is open and contains $\pi(z)$, it therefore contains its generalization $x$. Note that $\mathscr X$ is quasi-compact if and only if $X$ is quasi-compact. The finiteness follows.

label: eq:quotient-filtrations
title: Example
body_md:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ with an action of a smooth affine connected algebraic group $G$ over $k$ with a split maximal torus. By \cite[Thm. 1.4.8]{halpern-leistner2014instability} we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:quotient-filtrations}
\operatorname{Grad}([X/G]) \simeq \coprod_{\lambda} [X_\lambda/L_\lambda] \text{ and } \operatorname{Filt}([X/G]) \simeq \coprod_{\lambda}[X_\lambda^+/P_\lambda^+]
\end{equation}
where $\lambda$ runs through a complete set of conjugacy classes of $X_*(G)$. In particular, any connected component $Z \subseteq \operatorname{Grad}([X/G])$ is of the form $[F/L_\lambda]$ for some cocharacter $\lambda \in X_*(G)$ and connected component $F \in \pi_0(X_\lambda)$. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{gr}^{-1}(Z)=\operatorname{gr}^{-1}([F/L_\lambda])=[C_{\lambda,F}/P_\lambda^+],
\]
and if $X$ admits a good quotient $X \to X/G$ (cf. \Cref{rmk:ev1-closed-immersion}), then
\[
|\mathscr A_Z| = \operatorname{ev}_1(|\operatorname{gr}^{-1}(Z)|) = \operatorname{ev}_1([C_{\lambda,F}/P_\lambda^+]) = [G.C_{\lambda,F}/G] \subseteq [X/G].
\]

label: setup:locally-reductive
title: Setup
head: environment

label: prop:finite-images
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{prop:finite-images}
Assume the hypotheses of \Cref{setup:locally-reductive}. For every connected component $Z \in \pi_0(\operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X))$, the subset $|\mathscr A_Z| \subseteq |\mathscr X|$ is closed, and there are only finitely many distinct subsets of the form $|\mathscr A_Z|$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The finiteness assertion also follows from the reduction to affine torus quotients in \cite[Lem. 4.4.6 and proof of Lemm. 4.4.8]{halpern-leistner2014instability}. More generally, finiteness results for components of graded and filtered stacks, under the very mild hypothesis of quasi-compact graded points, are proved in \cite[Thms. 5.4.6 and 6.2.3]{BHIK2025}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{lem:adequate-charts}, there is an \'{e}tale cover $\{X_i \to X\}_i$ of $X$ by finitely many affine schemes and Cartesian presentations $\rho_i: \mathscr X_i:=[V_i/\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}] \to \mathscr X$ with $V_i$ affine and $n_i \geq 0$. The induced morphism $V_i \to \mathscr X_i \to X_i$ is a good quotient.

For every $k$-scheme $S$, the morphisms $\Theta_S \to S$ and
$\mathrm{B}\mathbb{G}_{m,S} \to S$ are good moduli spaces and hence universal for maps to algebraic spaces \cite[Thm. 6.6]{AlperGood}. So we obtain
\[
\operatorname{Filt}(\mathscr X_i) \simeq \operatorname{Filt}(\mathscr X) \times_X X_i \text{ and } \operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X_i) \simeq \operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X) \times_X X_i,
\]
compatible with $\operatorname{gr}$ and $\operatorname{ev}_1$. For a connected component $Z \in \pi_0(\operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X))$, we have a Cartesian diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
Z_i \ar[r,hook] \ar[d] & \operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X_i) \ar[d] \ar[r,hook,"\sigma_i"] & \operatorname{Filt}(\mathscr X_i) \ar[r,"\operatorname{ev}_1"] \ar[d] & \mathscr X_i \ar[r,"\pi_i"] \ar[d,"\rho_i"] & X_i \ar[d,"\text{\'{e}tale}"] \\
Z \ar[r,hook] & \operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X) \ar[r,hook,"\sigma"'] & \operatorname{Filt}(\mathscr X) \ar[r,"\operatorname{ev}_1"'] & \mathscr X \ar[r,"\pi"'] & X
\end{tikzcd}
\]
The pullback $Z_i:=Z \times_X X_i$ is a union of connected components of $\operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X_i)$. Since topological images commute with base change, we obtain 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lr-evaluation-base-change}
\rho_i^{-1}(|\mathscr A_Z|) = \bigcup_{Z' \in \pi_0(Z_i)}|\mathscr A_{Z'}|.
\end{equation}
By \eqref{eq:quotient-filtrations}, each connected component $Z'$ is of the form $[F/L_\lambda]$, and the preimage of $|\mathscr A_{Z'}| \subseteq |\mathscr X_i|$ in $V_i$ is $\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}.C_{\lambda,F}$. \Cref{lem:quotient-images} shows that there are only finitely many distinct $\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}$-saturations and each of them is closed in $V_i$. Thus the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:lr-evaluation-base-change} is a finite union of closed subsets in $|\mathscr X_i|$. Closedness descends along the \'{e}tale cover $\{\mathscr X_i \to \mathscr X\}_i$, so $|\mathscr A_Z| \subseteq |\mathscr X|$ is closed. On each \'{e}tale chart $\mathscr X_i \to \mathscr X$ there are only finitely many possible unions, and the finite cover determines a global subset $|\mathscr A_Z|$ by its pullbacks, proving finiteness.

title: Corollary
body_md:
Assume the hypotheses of \Cref{setup:locally-reductive}. Let $\mathscr D$ be an effective Cartier divisor on $\mathscr X$ and $\mathcal L:=\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(\mathscr D)$. For any $Z \in \pi_0(\operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X))$, we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item 
If $\operatorname{wt}(\mathcal L|_Z)<0$, then $\mathscr A_Z \subseteq \mathscr D$.
\item 
Let $e: \operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X) \xrightarrow{\sigma} \operatorname{Filt}(\mathscr X) \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_1} \mathscr X$ be the morphism forgetting the grading. If $e(|Z|) \cap |\mathscr D|=\varnothing$, then $\operatorname{wt}(\mathcal L|_Z)=0$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $s \in \Gamma(\mathscr X,\mathcal L)$ be the canonical section whose zero substack is $\mathscr D$.

(i). Suppose that $\operatorname{wt}(\mathcal L|_Z)<0$. Let $K/k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $f: \Theta_K \to \mathscr X$ be a filtration whose associated grading $f|_{\mathrm{B}\mathbb{G}_{m,K}}$ belongs to $Z$. By definition $\operatorname{wt}(f^*\mathcal L) = \operatorname{wt}(\mathcal L|_Z) < 0$. So $f$ factors through $\mathscr D$ by \Cref{cor:negative-in-D}. Consequently, $\operatorname{ev}_1(f)$ belongs to $\mathscr D$. Taking all such filtrations, and using the definition $|\mathscr A_Z| = \operatorname{ev}_1 \left( |\operatorname{gr}^{-1}(Z)| \right)$, we obtain $\mathscr A_Z \subseteq \mathscr D$.

(ii). Suppose that $e(|Z|) \cap |\mathscr D| = \varnothing$. Let $g: \mathrm{B}\mathbb{G}_{m,K} \to \mathscr X$ be any grading in $Z$. The underlying topological space of $\mathrm{B}\mathbb{G}_{m,K}$ consists of one point, whose image under $g$ is $e([g])$. Our assumption therefore implies that $g$ factors through $\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr D$. The canonical section $s$ is nowhere vanishing on this complement. Its pullback defines an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{B}\mathbb{G}_{m,K}} \xrightarrow{\sim} g^*\mathcal L$, sending $1 \mapsto g^*s$, of line bundles on $\mathrm{B}\mathbb{G}_{m,K}$. Hence $\operatorname{wt}(\mathcal L|_Z)=\operatorname{wt}(g^*\mathcal L)=0$, as required.

title: Theorem

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the \'{e}tale charts in the proof of \Cref{prop:finite-images}. Write $D_i$ for the pullback of $\mathscr D$ to $V_i$.  By \Cref{prop:chart-test}, $\mathscr D$ is removable for $\pi$ if and only if each $D_i$ is removable for $\pi_i$. By \Cref{thm:quotient-boundary}, the latter condition is equivalent to
\[
D_i = \bigcup_{\operatorname{wt}_\lambda(\mathcal O_{V_i}(D_i)|_F)<0}        \operatorname{GL}_{n_i}.C_{\lambda,F}.
\]
The equations \eqref{eq:lr-evaluation-base-change} and
\eqref{eq:lr-weight-comparison} identify these equalities with the
pullbacks of \eqref{eq:description-in-locally-reductive}, so they are equivalent to \eqref{eq:description-in-locally-reductive}.
The finiteness assertion follows from \Cref{prop:finite-images}.

label: cor:good-finite
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:good-finite}
Assume the hypotheses of \Cref{setup:locally-reductive}. Assume in addition that $\mathscr X$ is smooth. Then $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)$ is finite, and each element of $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)$ is of the form
\[
\mathscr A_Z \text{ with } \operatorname{wt}(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(\mathscr A_Z)|_Z)<0.
\]
Write $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)=\{\mathscr D_1,\ldots,\mathscr D_r\}$. For a subset $\sigma \subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}$, write
\[
\mathscr D_\sigma:=\sum_{i \in \sigma} \mathscr D_i \text{ and } \mathcal L_\sigma:=\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(\mathscr D_\sigma).
\]
Call $\sigma$ \emph{admissible} if, for every $i \in \sigma$, there exists $Z_i \in \pi_0(\operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X))$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:compatibility-weights}
\mathscr D_i=\mathscr A_{Z_i} \text{ and } \operatorname{wt}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_{Z_i})<0.
\end{equation}
The assignment $\sigma \mapsto \mathscr X \setminus \mathscr D_\sigma$ is an order-reversing bijection from admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,r\}$ to $\operatorname{Op}(\pi)$. In particular, we have $|\operatorname{Op}(\pi)| \leq 2^r$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\mathscr X$ is smooth, the stack $\operatorname{Filt}(\mathscr X)$ is smooth by \cite[Prop. 1.3.1 (4)]{halpern-leistner2014instability}. For each connected component
$Z \subseteq \operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X)$, the preimage $\operatorname{gr}^{-1}(Z)$ is smooth and connected, hence irreducible. Consequently, its image $\mathscr A_Z$ is irreducible.

By \Cref{thm:geometric-good} and \Cref{prop:finite-images}, every removable reduced Cartier boundary $\mathscr D_\sigma$ is a finite union of
closed irreducible substacks $\mathscr A_Z$ satisfying $\operatorname{wt}(\mathcal L_\sigma|_Z)<0$.
Each prime component $\mathscr D_i$ thus equals one of these $\mathscr A_Z$, proving \eqref{eq:compatibility-weights}. The remaining argument is identical to that of \Cref{cor:finite-reductive}.

title: Remark
body_md: In characteristic zero, it is possible to prove the finiteness of preserving opens using \cite[Cor. 4]{Benoist2013} (under normality in place of smoothness) and passage to \'{e}tale quotient charts.

label: ex:log-wall
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:log-wall}
We work over the field $\mathbb C$ of complex numbers. Following \cite{ADL}, let $\overline{\mathcal P}^{\mathrm{GIT}}_4$ denote the quotient stack of GIT-semistable plane quartics by $\operatorname{PGL}_3$, and let $\overline{\mathcal P}^{\mathrm{K}}_{4,3/8}$ denote the stack of K-semistable log Fano pairs admitting a $\mathbb Q$-Gorenstein smoothing to 
\[
\left( \mathbb P^2,\dfrac{3}{8}C \right)
\]
with $C$ a smooth plane quartic. Their good moduli spaces are denoted by $\overline{P}^{\mathrm{GIT}}_4$ and $\overline{P}^{\mathrm{K}}_{4,3/8}$, respectively. By \cite[Thm. 5.5]{ADL}, the first wall crossing gives an open immersion $\Phi^-: \overline{\mathcal P}^{\mathrm{GIT}}_4 \hookrightarrow \overline{\mathcal P}^{\mathrm K}_{4,3/8}$ inducing an isomorphism of good moduli spaces $\phi^-: \overline{P}^{\mathrm{GIT}}_4 \xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{P}^{\mathrm{K}}_{4,3/8}$. We describe its boundary using \Cref{thm:geometric-good}.

Let $\mathscr X:=\overline{\mathcal P}^{\mathrm{K}}_{4,3/8}$, identify $\mathscr U:=\overline{\mathcal P}^{\mathrm{GIT}}_4$ with its image, and write $\mathscr D:=(\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr U)_{\mathrm{red}}$. The geometric points of $\mathscr D$ are represented by
\[
\left( \mathbb P(1,1,4),\dfrac{3}{8} C_f \right) \text{ with } C_f=(z^2+f_8(x,y)=0) \text{ and } f_8 \in H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(8)),
\]
where $x,y,z$ have weights $1,1,4$. The distinguished K-polystable point is
\[
q=\left( \mathbb P(1,1,4),\dfrac{3}{8}Q'_4 \right) \text{ and } Q'_4=(z^2=0).
\]
The cocharacter
\[
\lambda: {\mathbb{G}_m} \to \operatorname{Aut}(q) \text{ given by } \lambda(t)[x:y:z]=[x:y:tz],
\]
gives the degeneration $z^2 + t^2 f_8(x,y)=0$ to $q$, as in \cite[Lem. 5.3 and its proof]{ADL}. More explicitly, setting
\[
H:=\operatorname{Aut}(q)=\operatorname{GL}_2 \times {\mathbb{G}_m} / \{(a\mathrm{I}_2,a^4): a \in {\mathbb{G}_m}\},
\]
we have $\mathscr D \simeq [H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(8))/H]$, with $\lambda$ acting on $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(8))$ with weight $2$. Let $Z \subseteq \operatorname{Grad}(\mathscr X)$ be the connected component containing the grading $(q,\lambda)$. Then $Z \simeq \mathrm{B}H$.

The weight of the normal line bundle can be read from the smoothing $u_0u_2-u_1^2 = sz \subseteq \mathbb P(1,1,1,2)$. The boundary is locally defined by $s=0$, so $\operatorname{wt}(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(\mathscr D)|_Z) = -1$. Every point of $\mathscr D$ has a degeneration with associated graded in $Z$, and the negative boundary weight gives $\mathscr A_Z \subseteq \mathscr D$. Consequently, $\mathscr A_Z=\mathscr D$ and $\operatorname{wt}(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(\mathscr D)|_Z)<0$. Thus this wall-crossing realizes a prime removable boundary in our classification.  Moreover, a computation of the attracting images shows that $\mathscr D$ is the unique codimension-one attracting image of $\mathscr X=\overline{\mathcal P}^{\mathrm K}_{4,3/8}$; hence, by \Cref{cor:good-finite}, $\overline{\mathcal P}^{\mathrm{GIT}}_4$ is the unique non-trivial open substack of $\mathscr X$ preserving its good moduli space.

title: Definition
body_md:
\label[definition]{defn:stable_adequate_moduli}
Let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space. A point $x$ of $\mathscr X$ is \emph{stable} relative to $\pi$ if $|\pi^{-1}(\pi(x))|=\{x\}$ under the induced map of topological spaces $|\mathscr X| \to |X|$. We say $\pi$ is a \emph{stable} adequate moduli space if there is an open dense set of stable points in $\mathscr X$.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space. The \emph{relative Picard group} is (as an abstract abelian group)
\[
\operatorname{Pic}(\mathscr X/X):=\operatorname{coker} \bigl( \pi^*: \operatorname{Pic}(X) \to \operatorname{Pic}(\mathscr X) \bigr)
\]
and denote its rank by $\rho_\pi:=\operatorname{rk} \operatorname{Pic}(\mathscr X/X)$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: By the projection formula and $\pi_*\mathcal O_\mathscr X = \mathcal O_X$, the pullback $\pi^*: \operatorname{Pic}(X) \to \operatorname{Pic}(\mathscr X)$ is injective. Note that $[\mathcal L] \in \operatorname{Pic}(\mathscr X/X)$ is torsion precisely when some positive power of $\mathcal L$ descends to $X$.

label: lem:adequate-power-descent
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:adequate-power-descent}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an adequate moduli space, where $\mathscr X$ is an algebraic stack of finite type over $k$. Let $\mathcal L$ be a line bundle on $\mathscr X$. Suppose that, for every geometric point $x \in |\mathscr X|$ with closed image, the stabilizer $G_x$ acts trivially on $\mathcal L_x$. Then there exists an integer $n>0$ such that $\mathcal L^{\otimes n} \simeq \pi^*M$ for some line bundle $M$ on $X$.
head: environment
name: Descent up to a power

title: Proof
body_md:
Adequate moduli spaces are preserved by flat base change \cite[Prop. 5.2.9 (1)]{AlperAdequate}, and descent of a line bundle along an adequate moduli space is fpqc-local on the target \cite[Lem. 5.1.5]{MR5066465}. Since $X$ is quasi-compact, we may work over an \'{e}tale cover of $X$ by finitely many affine schemes and take a common multiple of the resulting exponents. So hereafter we may assume that $X$ is affine.

Fix a closed point $y \in X$, and let $x$ be the unique closed point of $\pi^{-1}(y)$ (see \cite[Thm. 5.3.1]{AlperAdequate}). Since $y$ is closed, $x$ is also closed in $\mathscr X$. Its residual gerbe $i: \mathrm{B}G_x \hookrightarrow \mathscr X$ is therefore a closed immersion. By hypothesis, $i^*\mathcal L$ is trivial. Choose a nowhere-vanishing section $t$ of $i^*\mathcal L$. Consider the surjection of graded quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_\mathscr X$-algebras
\[
\bigoplus_{d \geq 0} \mathcal L^{\otimes d} \twoheadrightarrow i_*\bigoplus_{d \geq 0}i^*\mathcal L^{\otimes d}.
\]
By adequacy, some positive power of $t$ lifts to a global section of $\bigoplus_{d \geq 0} \mathcal L^{\otimes d}$. Taking its homogeneous component of the appropriate degree gives an integer $n_y>0$ and a section (see \cite[Lem. 4.1.8]{AlperAdequate}) $s_y \in \Gamma(\mathscr X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n_y})$ such that $i^*s_y=t^{n_y}$. The zero locus $\mathbf{V}(s_y)$ does not contain $x$, and hence is disjoint from $\pi^{-1}(y)$. Since $\pi$ is closed, the subset $U_y:=X \setminus \pi(\mathbf{V}(s_y)) \subseteq X$ is an open neighborhood of $y$, and $s_y$ trivializes $\mathcal L^{\otimes n_y}$ on $\pi^{-1}(U_y)$. These neighborhoods cover all closed points of $X$, and hence cover $X$. Choose a finite subcover $U_{y_1},\dots,U_{y_r}$ of $X$, and let $n$ be a common multiple of $n_{y_1},\dots,n_{y_r}$. Then $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is trivial over every open $\pi^{-1}(U_{y_i})$, so it descends to $X$ by \cite[Lem. 5.1.5 (ii)]{MR5066465}.
head: environment

label: prop:relative-picard-finiteness
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:relative-picard-finiteness}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be an
adequate moduli space, where $\mathscr X$ is an algebraic stack of finite type
over $k$ with affine diagonal. Then the quotient $\Lambda_\pi:=\operatorname{Pic}(\mathscr X/X)/\operatorname{Pic}(\mathscr X/X)_{\operatorname{tors}}$ is a free abelian group of finite rank. In particular, we have $\rho_\pi < \infty$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose an atlas $U \twoheadrightarrow \mathscr X$ with $U$ a scheme of finite type over $k$. By generic flatness and noetherian induction, $U_{\mathrm{red}}$
admits a finite stratification $U_{\mathrm{red}}=\sqcup_{i} U_i$ by integral locally closed subschemes
$U_i$ such that $H_i:=\mathcal I_{\mathscr X} \times_{\mathscr X} U_i \to U_i$ is flat, where $\mathcal I_{\mathscr X}$ is the inertia stack of $\mathscr X$. Let $\eta_i$ be a geometric generic point of $U_i$, and let $G_i:=(H_i)_{\eta_i}$. Stabilizer actions on the fibers of line bundles induce a homomorphism
\[
w: \operatorname{Pic}(\mathscr X/X) \to \bigoplus_i X^*(G_i)/X^*(G_i)_{\operatorname{tors}}.
\]
The target is free of finite rank, since each $X^*(G_i)$ is finitely
generated \cite[Lem. 4.9]{MR3503967}. To conclude, we show that $\ker w = \operatorname{Pic}(\mathscr X/X)_{\operatorname{tors}}$, and hence $\Lambda_\pi$ embeds into a free abelian group of finite rank and is therefore itself is free of finite rank.

Suppose that $w([\mathcal L])=0$.  We show $\mathcal L$ is torsion. By definition, there exists an integer $m>0$ such that the character of stabilizer at $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ is trivial at every generic point $\eta_i$. Since $H_i$ is flat over the integral scheme $U_i$, the corresponding character $H_i \to \mathbb{G}_{m,U_i}$ is trivial everywhere. Thus every geometric stabilizer of $\mathscr X$ acts trivially on $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$. By \Cref{lem:adequate-power-descent}, some positive power of $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ descends to $X$, so $\mathcal L$ itself is torsion.

label: thm:stack-picard-bound
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:stack-picard-bound}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $\mathscr X$ be a smooth locally reductive integral algebraic stack of finite type over $k$ with affine diagonal, and let $\pi: \mathscr X \to X$ be a stable adequate moduli space. Then
\[
|\mathrm{PD}(\pi)| \leq 2 \rho_\pi \text{ and } |\operatorname{Op}(\pi)| \leq 3^{\rho_\pi}.
\]
Both upper bounds are sharp.
head: environment

label: claim:function-field-equal
title: Proof
body_md:
By \cite[Thm. 5.3.1 and Prop. 5.4.1]{AlperAdequate}, the morphism $\pi$ is surjective and universally closed, and $X$ is integral. In particular, the pullback $\pi^*: k(X) \to k(\mathscr X)$ is injective. Since $\pi$ is also stable, actually we have
\begin{claim}\label{claim:function-field-equal}
The pullback $\pi^*: k(X) \xrightarrow{\sim} k(\mathscr X)$ is an isomorphism.
\end{claim}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Claim \ref{claim:function-field-equal}]
Let $f \in k(\mathscr X)$, and choose an open dense substack $\mathscr U \subseteq \mathscr X$ on which $f$ is regular. Since stable points are dense, there is a stable point $x \in |\mathscr U|$. The fiber over $\pi(x)$ consists only of $x$ itself, so $U:=X \setminus \pi(\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr U) \subseteq X$ is a non-empty open subset of $X$ with $\pi^{-1}(U) \subseteq \mathscr U$.
Then $\mathcal O_X \simeq \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$ gives $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X) \xrightarrow{\sim} \Gamma(\pi^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$. This shows that $f|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}$ is pulled back from a regular function on $U$, proving that $f$ lies in the image of $k(X)$.
\end{proof}
Suppose $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)=\{\mathscr D_1,\dots,\mathscr D_{r}\}$. Consider the morphism
\[
\alpha: \mathbb Q^{r} \to \operatorname{Pic}(\mathscr X/X) \otimes_{\mathbb Z} \mathbb Q \text{ sending } e_i \mapsto [\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(\mathscr D_i)].
\]
where $e_i$ is the $i$-th standard basis vector. For any $a=(a_i) \in \ker \alpha$, by definition there exists an integer $n>0$ such that $\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}\left(n \sum_{i=1}^{r} a_i \mathscr D_i\right) \simeq \pi^*L$ for some line bundle $L$ on $X$.
\begin{claim}\label{claim:unique-B-on-X}
There exists a unique $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{r} a_i\mathscr D_i=\pi^*D$.
\end{claim}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Claim \ref{claim:unique-B-on-X}]
Let $\mathscr D:=\sum_{i=1}^{r} a_i \mathscr D_i$, and fix an isomorphism $\varphi: \mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D) \xrightarrow{\sim} \pi^*L$. Let $\sigma_{n\mathscr D}$ be the canonical rational section of $\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D)$, so that $\operatorname{div}(\sigma_{n\mathscr D})=n\mathscr D$, and choose a non-zero
rational section $s$ of $L$. Consider $g:=\varphi(\sigma_{n\mathscr D})/\pi^*s \in k(\mathscr X)^\times$. Since $\pi^*:k(X) \xrightarrow{\sim} k(\mathscr X)$ is an isomorphism by Claim \ref{claim:function-field-equal}, there is a unique $f \in k(X)^\times$ such that $g=\pi^*f$. Hence $\varphi(\sigma_{n\mathscr D})=\pi^*(fs)$. Taking divisors of rational sections gives $n\mathscr D =\operatorname{div} \bigl(\varphi(\sigma_{n\mathscr D})\bigr)=\pi^*\operatorname{div}(fs)$. Define $D:=\operatorname{div}(fs)/n=\bigl(\operatorname{div}(s)+\operatorname{div}(f)\bigr)/n$, and it is a $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor satisfying $\mathscr D=\pi^*D$.
\end{proof}
Note that for any prime divisor $E$ on $X$, the closure of every irreducible component of $\pi^{-1}(\eta_E)$ in $\mathscr X$ has codimension one. Let $D_1,\dots,D_q$ be the prime divisors on $X$ such that the closure of each irreducible component of $\pi^{-1}(\eta_{D_j})$ in $\mathscr X$, equipped with its reduced structure, is one of the $\mathscr D_i$. For $j=1,\dots,q$, set
\[
I_j:=\{i \in \{1,\dots,r\}: \pi(\mathscr D_i)=D_j\}.
\]
The sets $I_j$ are pairwise disjoint and $|I_j| \geq 2$. Indeed, if $I_j=\{i\}$, then $\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr D_i$ would have empty fiber over $\eta_{D_j}$, contradicting the surjectivity required by removability. Note that this gives a subset $\sqcup_{j=1}^q I_j \subseteq \mathrm{PD}(\pi)$ and hence
\[
r=|\mathrm{PD}(\pi)| \geq \sum_{j=1}^q |I_j| \geq \sum_{j=1}^q 2 = 2q.
\]

For the $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor $D$ on $X$ in Claim \ref{claim:unique-B-on-X}, every component of $\operatorname{Supp}(D)$ is one of the $D_j$. Since $X$ is normal \cite[Prop. 5.4.1]{AlperAdequate}, the divisor $D$ is uniquely determined by its coefficients along $D_1,\dots,D_q$. Therefore
\[
\dim_{\mathbb Q} \ker \alpha \leq q \text{ and hence } r-q \leq \rho_\pi.
\]
Combining this with $r \ge 2q$, we obtain $r \leq 2 \rho_\pi$. 

By \Cref{cor:good-finite}, every preserving open corresponds to a unique subset of $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)$, and a subset of $\mathrm{PD}(\pi)$ defining a preserving open cannot contain all of $I_j$, as the complement would miss the fiber over $\eta_{D_j}$. This observation gives an upper bound
\[
|\operatorname{Op}(\pi)| \leq 2^{r-\sum_{j=1}^q |I_j|} \prod_{j=1}^q \left(2^{|I_j|}-1\right) \leq 3^{r-\sum_{j=1}^q |I_j|} \prod_{j=1}^q \left(3^{|I_j|-1}\right) = 3^{r-q} \leq 3^{\rho_\pi},
\]
where we use $2^k-1 \leq 3^{k-1}$ for $k \geq 2$. Sharpness is achieved by \Cref{ex:axes} as $\operatorname{Pic}([\mathbb A^{2r}/\mathbb T]) \simeq X^*(\mathbb T) \simeq \mathbb Z^r$ and $\operatorname{Pic}(\mathbb A^r)=0$, so we have $\rho_\pi=r$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f \in k(\mathscr X)$, and choose an open dense substack $\mathscr U \subseteq \mathscr X$ on which $f$ is regular. Since stable points are dense, there is a stable point $x \in |\mathscr U|$. The fiber over $\pi(x)$ consists only of $x$ itself, so $U:=X \setminus \pi(\mathscr X \setminus \mathscr U) \subseteq X$ is a non-empty open subset of $X$ with $\pi^{-1}(U) \subseteq \mathscr U$.
Then $\mathcal O_X \simeq \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$ gives $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X) \xrightarrow{\sim} \Gamma(\pi^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$. This shows that $f|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}$ is pulled back from a regular function on $U$, proving that $f$ lies in the image of $k(X)$.

label: claim:unique-B-on-X
title: Claim
body_md:
\label{claim:unique-B-on-X}
There exists a unique $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{r} a_i\mathscr D_i=\pi^*D$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathscr D:=\sum_{i=1}^{r} a_i \mathscr D_i$, and fix an isomorphism $\varphi: \mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D) \xrightarrow{\sim} \pi^*L$. Let $\sigma_{n\mathscr D}$ be the canonical rational section of $\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}(n\mathscr D)$, so that $\operatorname{div}(\sigma_{n\mathscr D})=n\mathscr D$, and choose a non-zero
rational section $s$ of $L$. Consider $g:=\varphi(\sigma_{n\mathscr D})/\pi^*s \in k(\mathscr X)^\times$. Since $\pi^*:k(X) \xrightarrow{\sim} k(\mathscr X)$ is an isomorphism by Claim \ref{claim:function-field-equal}, there is a unique $f \in k(X)^\times$ such that $g=\pi^*f$. Hence $\varphi(\sigma_{n\mathscr D})=\pi^*(fs)$. Taking divisors of rational sections gives $n\mathscr D =\operatorname{div} \bigl(\varphi(\sigma_{n\mathscr D})\bigr)=\pi^*\operatorname{div}(fs)$. Define $D:=\operatorname{div}(fs)/n=\bigl(\operatorname{div}(s)+\operatorname{div}(f)\bigr)/n$, and it is a $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor satisfying $\mathscr D=\pi^*D$.

label: prop:reductive-picard-comparison
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{prop:reductive-picard-comparison}
There is an exact sequence
\[
X^*(G)_{\mathbb Q} \xrightarrow{\beta} (\operatorname{Pic}^G(X)/\pi^*\operatorname{Pic}(Y))_{\mathbb Q} \xrightarrow{\mathrm F} (\operatorname{Pic}(X)/q^*\operatorname{Pic}(Y))_{\mathbb Q} \to 0,
\]
where $\beta(\chi)=\mathcal O_X(\chi)$, with $\mathcal O_X(\chi)$ the trivial line bundle with the $G$-linearization given by $\chi$, and $\mathrm F$ is the forgetful map. If $X^G \neq \varnothing$, this extends to a split short exact sequence
\[
0 \to X^*(G)_{\mathbb Q} \xrightarrow{\beta} (\operatorname{Pic}^G(X)/\pi^*\operatorname{Pic}(Y))_{\mathbb Q}
\xrightarrow{\mathrm F} (\operatorname{Pic}(X)/q^*\operatorname{Pic}(Y))_{\mathbb Q} \to 0.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cite[Prop. 2.10 and Thm. 2.14]{Brion}, there is an exact sequence
\[
X^*(G)_{\mathbb Q} \to \operatorname{Pic}^G(X)_{\mathbb Q} \xrightarrow{\mathrm F} \operatorname{Pic}(X)_{\mathbb Q} \to 0.
\]
The forgetful map $\mathrm F$ carries $\pi^*\operatorname{Pic}(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ onto $q^*\operatorname{Pic}(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$, so passing to the quotients gives the first sequence. If $x \in X^G(k)$, taking the character of the $G$-action
on the fiber at $x$ defines a morphism $\operatorname{wt}_x: \operatorname{Pic}^G(X) \to X^*(G)$. It vanishes on $\pi^*\operatorname{Pic}(Y)$ and sends $\mathcal O_X(\chi)$ to $\chi$. Passing to the quotients and tensoring with $\mathbb Q$, it therefore gives a section of $\beta$, proving the second assertion.

label: cor:reductive-relative-picard-comparison
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:reductive-relative-picard-comparison}
We have $\rho_q+\operatorname{rk} G/[G,G] \geq \rho_\pi \geq \rho_q$. If in addition $X^G \neq \varnothing$, then $\rho_\pi=\rho_q+\operatorname{rk} G/[G,G]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Take ranks in \Cref{prop:reductive-picard-comparison}, using $\operatorname{rk} X^*(G)=\operatorname{rk} G/[G,G]$.

label: cor:ordinary-picard-counting
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:ordinary-picard-counting}
Assume that $X^s \neq \varnothing$. Then
\[
|\mathrm{PD}(q)| \leq 2(\rho_q+\operatorname{rk} G/[G,G]) \text{ and } |\operatorname{Op}(q)| \leq 3^{\rho_q+\operatorname{rk} G/[G,G]}.
\]
If in addition $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is torsion, then
\[
|\mathrm{PD}(q)| \leq 2\operatorname{rk} G/[G,G] \text{ and } |\operatorname{Op}(q)| \leq 3^{\operatorname{rk} G/[G,G]}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Follows from \Cref{thm:stack-picard-bound} and \Cref{cor:reductive-relative-picard-comparison}. If $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is torsion, then $\rho_q=0$.

label: ex:torus-no-stable-unbounded
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:torus-no-stable-unbounded}
The assumption $X^s \neq \varnothing$ in \Cref{cor:ordinary-picard-counting} cannot be omitted in general, even for torus actions on affine space. Indeed, let $n \geq 3$, and let $\mathbb T=\mathbb{G}_m^3$ act on $X=\mathbb A^n$ by
\[
(s,t,u).(x_j)_{j=0}^{n-1}:=\bigl(st^ju^{j^2}x_j\bigr)_{j=0}^{n-1}.
\]
The origin is the unique closed orbit, and $X^s=\varnothing$, and the good quotient is $q: X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$. Since $\operatorname{Pic}(X)=0$ and the origin is fixed, \Cref{cor:reductive-relative-picard-comparison} gives $\rho_q=0$ and $\rho_\pi=3$.

For each $i$, let $U_i:=\mathbf{D}(x_i) \subseteq X$ and consider the cocharacter $\lambda_i(z)=(z^{i^2},z^{-2i},z)$. The $\lambda_i$-weight on $x_j$ is $(j-i)^2$, so $k[U_i]^{\lambda_i}=k[x_i^{\pm 1}]$. Since the first factor of $\mathbb T$ scales $x_i$, it follows that
$k[U_i]^\mathbb T=k$. Thus each affine open $U_i \subseteq X$ preserves $q$,
and all $n$ coordinate hyperplanes are removable. Therefore
\[
|\mathrm{PD}(q)|\geq n \text{ and } |\operatorname{Op}(q)|\geq n+1.
\]
Neither is bounded by the relative Picard rank.

label: lem:generalgm
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:generalgm}
Assume $G={\mathbb{G}_m}$. If $X^s=\varnothing$, then $|\mathrm{PD}(q)| \leq 1 \leq 2\rho_\pi$ and $|\operatorname{Op}(q)| \leq 2 \leq 3^{\rho_\pi}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Since $X^s=\varnothing$, we have $X=\cup_i X_i^\pm$, and each $X_i^\pm$ is closed in $X$. Irreducibility therefore gives $X=X_i^+$ or $X=X_i^-$ for some $i$. In particular, the fixed locus $X^{{\mathbb{G}_m}}$ is non-empty and connected. By \Cref{thm:main-Gm}, the only possible non-trivial open preserving $q$ is $X \setminus X^{{\mathbb{G}_m}}$. This proves the first two bounds. Finally, by \Cref{cor:reductive-relative-picard-comparison} we have $\rho_\pi=\rho_q+1\geq1$, proving the remaining inequalities.

label: prop:fixed-weight-kernel
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:fixed-weight-kernel}
We have $\Lambda_\pi \hookrightarrow \mathbb Z^m$ and hence $m \geq \rho_\pi$.

label: thm:fixed-components
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:fixed-components}
Assume that $\operatorname{codim}_X X_i \leq 3$ for each $i \in \pi_0(X^{\mathbb{G}_m})$. Then $m=\rho_\pi$. If in addition $X^{\mathbb{G}_m} \neq \varnothing$, then $m=1+\rho_q$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $m \leq 1$, the equality follows from \Cref{prop:fixed-weight-kernel}. Suppose $m \geq 2$, and let
\[
p_i:=\operatorname{codim}_X X_i^- \text{ and } q_i:=\operatorname{codim}_X X_i^+.
\]
The loci $X_i^\pm$ are closed in $X$. Thus $p_i=0$ or $q_i=0$
would force the corresponding locus to equal $X$ and hence
$X_i=X^{\mathbb{G}_m}$, contradicting $m \geq 2$. Therefore
\[
p_i, q_i \geq 1 \text{ and } p_i+q_i=\operatorname{codim}_X X_i \leq 3.
\]
In particular, at least one of $X_i^\pm$ is a divisor. If $X_i^+$ is a divisor, then the weight of the line bundle $\mathcal O_X(X_i^+)$ is $0$ on each $X_j$ with $j \neq i$ and non-zero on $X_i$, by \Cref{cor:weight-inclusion}. Hence $w(\mathcal O_X(X_i^+))=c_i e_i$ for some $c_i \neq 0$. These $m$ vectors are linearly independent, so $m \geq \rho_\pi \geq m$, i.e., $m=\rho_\pi$. If $X^{\mathbb{G}_m} \neq \varnothing$, then $m=1+\rho_q$ follows from \Cref{cor:reductive-relative-picard-comparison}.

label: cor:fixed-torsion-picard
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:fixed-torsion-picard}
Assume that $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is torsion (e.g., $X=\operatorname{Spec} A$ for some UFD $A$). Then $|\operatorname{Op}(q)| \leq 3$. If in addition $\dim X \leq 3$, then $X^{\mathbb{G}_m}$ is either empty or irreducible.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: By \Cref{cor:reductive-relative-picard-comparison} we have $\rho_\pi \leq 1$, and hence $|\operatorname{Op}(q)| \leq 3$. If $X^{\mathbb{G}_m} \neq \varnothing$, then by \Cref{thm:fixed-components} we have $m=1+\rho_q=1$.
